J1.evidence: «وقُرِىء تَسْقيكم بالتاءِ مِنْ فوقُ» - «مِنْ فوقُ» is only the Arabic letter-disambiguator (tāʾ with dots above vs yāʾ/nūn); in Latin transliteration 'with the tāʾ' already names exactly that letter, so no content or meaning is lost and nothing is wrong. Rest of EN («أي: الأنعام» -> 'the cattle (al-anʿām)') faithful.

J2.evidence: «وقُرِىء تَسْقيكم بالتاءِ مِنْ فوقُ أي: الأنعام»: 'من فوق' is the standard way of saying the letter is tāʾ (ت, dotted above) and not yāʾ; EN 'with the tāʾ' already names exactly that letter, and the Arabic form «تَسْقيكم» is quoted, so no information is lost. Meaning complete; an explicit '(dotted above)' would be optional stylistic gain, not a fix of an error.
